target_customer: Patients with CLN1 Batten disease and later other neurodegenerative diseases, reached through drug development funded by grants and investors, with pharma partners as eventual payers
problem: CLN1 Batten disease is an ultra-rare fatal childhood neurodegenerative disease with no approved disease modifying therapy; the company targets protein palmitoylation as a route to treat it and related diseases.
business_model: Preclinical biotech drug development funded by NIH grants and equity, aiming to license or develop drugs

founders.name: Devin Wiley
founders.background_notes: Only founder on the YC page; a directory listing calls him MD PhD, chief medical officer and head of R&D, not confirmed from a primary source. Education and prior employers not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Drug discovery for a rare neurodegenerative disease needs preclinical efficacy, toxicology and an IND before any human data; the lead program had not reached clinical trials.

defensibility.rationale: Patent and orphan drug style protection can be strong once a candidate exists, but at founding the science was unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent was found building the same palmitoylation approach; gene and enzyme therapies for CLN1 were being developed by others, with dated evidence only from 2019.

market_need_then: No approved disease modifying therapy exists for CLN1 Batten disease according to the 2020 review and news found; NIH funded several SBIR grants to the company from 2017.

branding.domain_note: Company site at circumventpharmaceuticals.com, not the bare name
branding.community_and_virality: Partnerships with Batten disease patient organizations are mentioned on the company site

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found; it is a scientific biotech with a small public profile.

outcome_analysis: Circumvent is still listed as active with six people at YC and a lead program for CLN1 Batten disease, funded mostly by NIH SBIR grants since 2017. No clinical trial had started in the sources found, no exit has been reported and no equity round could be verified, so the outcome is still open.
notes: Aggregators disagree on totals (7.93M across five rounds, 3.7M across three, 150K). SBIR.gov rollup via a search snippet showed about 5.1M in five NIH awards, only the first 2017 award is recorded as a round. A 6.0M seed in June 2025 is unverified, no Form D found. The YC investor link is from aggregators only. Competitor evidence for CLN1 programs (Abeona, May 2019) is dated too long after the batch, so the list is empty. No outcome or shutdown news was found.
